summary: The three-large-eigenvalue hypothesis does not force a positive universal aggregate indefinite-pair Schur currency. For P=2[[1,1,1],[1,1,-1],[1,-1,1]] and C_eps=eps[[1,0],[0,1],[0,0]], 0<eps<=1/2, A_eps=[[P,C_eps],[C_eps^T,0_2]] has at least three eigenvalues of modulus >=1 by Weyl, while every 2x2 principal block of P is singular with eigenvalues {0,4}, so the eligible indefinite-pair aggregate currency is zero. This refutes only pair-resource forcing, not QFORM; singular/definite-pair survivors require another route.
